answer: At most 5 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a bridge tag. The velvet cap is enforced at intake and opal publishes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a fleet in one epoch however much capital it holds, because each account consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 29 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
